articles.title: El Heliodoro despide a De Miguel en un adiós que une a todo el fútbol entre lágrimas, recuerdos y dolor
articles.standfirst: El Tenerife celebra un solemne homenaje al delantero fallecido en el que estuvieron representados todos los clubes de Primera y Segunda
articles.summary: El Tenerife celebra un solemne homenaje al delantero fallecido en el que estuvieron representados todos los clubes de Primera y Segunda
articles.body: El Heliodoro Rodríguez López volvió a ser una familia. Sin fútbol, sin goles que celebrar y sin un balón que echar a rodar. Con el corazón encogido y un nombre que resonó en las gradas como si todavía estuviera sobre el césped, el de Jesús de Miguel. El Tenerife despidió este sábado, en un acto que prácticamente duró dos horas, con representación de todos los clubes de Primera y Segunda división, a uno de los suyos en un homenaje cargado de emoción, de dolor, de lágrimas, de recuerdos y de ese cariño que permanece cuando alguien se marcha demasiado pronto. Las largas colas para acceder al estadio anticiparon la dimensión del sentimiento blanquiazul. La amenaza de la tormenta Bruna, sin embargo, impidió que el recinto se llenara. Muchos optaron por quedarse en casa, pero quienes acudieron encontraron un Heliodoro diferente. El silencio reinó durante buena parte del acto, interrumpido únicamente por aplausos que brotaban desde el alma. Y, de pronto, el nombre de Demi. Coreado con fuerza, sin necesidad de que hubiera un balón en juego. Porque también hay días en los que la afición acude al estadio para algo mucho más importante que el fútbol. La puerta 9, el dorsal que defendió Jesús de Miguel, se convirtió en un océano de flores. Un lugar de encuentro para quienes quisieron dejarle un último mensaje, una despedida o simplemente permanecer unos minutos junto a su recuerdo. Allí, entre bufandas, camisetas, velas y ramos, el Tenerife encontró una manera de abrazar a quien ya no podrá volver a vestir su camiseta. Enric Gallego, capitán del equipo, puso voz al dolor de un vestuario todavía incapaz de asumir la ausencia. “Es muy difícil estar aquí. Nadie está preparado para estar aquí en un momento como este, ni encontrar las palabras para despedir a alguien que estuvo hasta el otro día en el vestuario”, reconoció antes de dejar una promesa que atravesó el estadio, “siempre serás uno de los nuestros”. El delantero quiso recordar al futbolista, pero también a la persona que había detrás de la camiseta. A ese compañero “natural y cercano” que seguirá presente cada vez que el equipo entre en el vestuario o salte al campo. “Los partidos terminan, las temporadas pasan y las camisetas se defienden. Tú seguirás formando parte de nuestras vidas para siempre”, añadió para agradecer a la afición y al club su manera de acompañar al equipo. “Esto es mucho más que un club. Es una familia”. Felipe Miñambres, presidente del Tenerife, recordó al Jesús de Miguel que conocía mucho antes de su llegada a la isla. Un futbolista tímido, introvertido, de los que parecen no estar, pero siempre están. “Era alguien cercano para los que lo necesitaban. Era una persona que no pedía, sino de las que daban”, evocó. “Su timidez desaparecía dentro del área, donde ya no habrá más goles, pero sí un recuerdo que permanecerá para siempre”. Rayco García, máximo accionista de la entidad, tampoco encontró palabras suficientes para explicar una pérdida que ha golpeado a toda la familia blanquiazul. Agradeció la atención médica recibida, el respaldo del fútbol nacional e internacional y el cariño de una afición que ha demostrado estar a la altura de las circunstancias. También tuvo palabras para la UD Las Palmas y Miguel Ángel Ramírez, en un gesto de agradecimiento que trascendió cualquier rivalidad. Y, sobre todo, dejó una promesa. Carla, la hija de Jesús, nunca estará sola. El Tenerife se encargará de que conozca quién fue su padre y lo que significó defender aquella camiseta. “No vamos a permitir que le falte de nada”, aseguró, emocionado, antes de trasladar al vestuario el orgullo de toda una isla. La jornada terminó con el mensaje de una familia profundamente conmovida por tantas muestras de afecto. Cada palabra, cada abrazo y cada gesto habían servido para aliviar, siquiera por un instante, un dolor imposible de medir. “Cuando el dolor se comparte, el amor se multiplica”, recordaron los familiares en una misiva que fue leída por el conductor del acto, José Manuel Pitti. Y eso fue precisamente lo que sucedió en el Heliodoro Rodríguez López. Tenerife compartió su tristeza, se abrazó en el recuerdo y convirtió una despedida en una declaración de cariño. Jesús de Miguel ya no estará en el vestuario ni volverá a celebrar un gol con el conjunto blanquiazul. Pero su nombre seguirá teniendo un lugar en las gradas, en la puerta 9 y en el corazón de quienes, este sábado, le dijeron adiós sin dejar de sentirlo cerca.

articles.title: Angel Reese, Paul Skenes, Shaq Join Lane Kiffin for Victory Hill Walk in Video Ahead of LSU-Alabama
articles.summary: Some Tigers legends are in Death Valley for a Saturday evening matchup between No. 15 LSU and No. 9 Alabama.
articles.body:
Some Tigers legends are in Death Valley for a Saturday evening matchup between No. 15 LSU and No. 9 Alabama.

Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese, Pittsburgh Pirates ace Paul Skenes, Basketball Hall of Famer Shaquille O'Neal and actor and filmmaker Kevin Costner joined head coach Lane Kiffin for his walk down Victory Hill in a video shared by WAFB-TV's Jacques Doucet.

Alabama (6-2) was ranked No. 5 in the first rankings shared by the College Football Playoff selection committee, while LSU (6-2) came in at No. 14.

A victory over Alabama on Saturday would go a long way toward convincing the selection committee that the Tigers deserve a spot in the final playoff bracket.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest 3-1 Man City: How the players rated
articles.summary: How Nottingham Forest and Manchester City's players rated following their Premier League match at the City Ground.
articles.body:
Liam Delap scored twice against his old club to help Nottingham Forest to victory and inflict a third straight Premier League loss on Manchester City .

Here's how I rated the players and and you can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Matz Sels: Could do nothing about Rayan Cherki's goal. 6

Daniel Munoz: Looked pumped and did superbly to keep the dangerous Jeremy Doku quiet. 7

Jair Cunha: The centre-back found himself in attack in the sixth minute, when he pounced before coolly rolling in the opener. Made a brilliant goalline clearance at the other end. 8

Nikola Milenkovic: Stood tall to block a Jeremy Doku strike early on which epitomised his overall showing. 7

Murillo: The Brazilian was solid and did what was asked of him, to help stop Erling Haaland. 7

Neco Williams: Got stuck in when required. A solid performance. 7

Ryan Yates: The captain's poor clearance allowed Cherki to score in the second half. 6

Xaver Schlager: Provided the assist for the second goal in a decent showing. 7

James McAtee: Had a very good game against his former club. Could have enjoyed a goal but had a weak shot saved, before blazing another over. 7

Morgan Gibbs-White: Hard-working and caused City a few problems in the final third. 7

Liam Delap: A double for the no-nonsense ex-City striker. Two thunderous finishes brought the stadium alive. 9

Subs not used: John Victor, Ousmane Diomande, Callum Hudson-Odoi, Chris Wood, Arnaud Kalimuendo.

Gianluigi Donnarumma: Another game without a clean sheet, another three conceded. Aerially suspect too. Not having a good season. 4

Abdukodir Khusanov: Seems awkward when shunted out to the right, before being moved back inside. 4

Ruben Dias: A desperate lunge to try to block Delap's goal summed up his - and his side's - poor display. 4

Marc Guehi: Part of a City defence that were all over the place in the first half before being hooked at half-time. 4

Josko Gvardiol: Not in great form at the moment. Soft on the ball early on when he had his pocket picked by Cunha for Forest's opener and was also substituted. 4

Elliot Anderson: Made an unhappy return to the City Ground where he lost the midfield battle. 5

Enzo Fernandez: A really disappointing performance. Should have pulled a goal back but sent his header from close range over. Midfield seems to lack in balance with him and Anderson in the side. 5

Jeremy Doku: Got no change out of Munoz and produced very little. 5

Iliman Ndiaye: Missed interception led to Forest's second goal and did not contribute much in attack. Not his best game. 5

Rayan Cherki: Pulled a goal back for City with a stunning finish in the second half. 6

Erling Haaland: Had some chances but not his best showing in front of goal. 5

Matheus Nunes (on 45, Guehi) Failed to put a foot in on Delap for Forest's third. 5

Nico O'Reilly (on 45, Gvardiol) With Gvardiol shaky, will the Englishman be given a run of games in the side? 6

Subs not used: Geronimo Rulli, Mateo Kovacic, Vitor Reis, Ayyoub Bouaddi, Allan, Rico Lewis.

After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.

articles.title: El Córdoba se viene arriba: 3-0 al Ceuta y 10 de los últimos 12 puntos en juego
articles.standfirst: Percan firmó un doblete y ya suma media docena de goles en Liga
articles.summary: Percan firmó un doblete y ya suma media docena de goles en Liga
articles.body: El Córdoba logró su tercera victoria en los cuatro últimos partidos y sigue progresando en puestos y sensaciones tras vencer a un Ceuta que pagó su falta de gol, con varias ocasiones desaprovechadas. Un autogol de Anuar y un doblete de Diego Percan, con dedicatoria a su compañero fallecido Jesús de Miguel, sentenciaron al colista de Segunda. Pareció como si Córdoba y Ceuta no fueran en serio en el encuentro hasta llegar y vivir un emotivo minuto 9 de recuerdo a Jesús de Miguel. Justo en la reanudación del envite, Carracedo lanzó un libre directo que sacó Pedro López de la escuadra. Los caballas replicaron con un disparo de Escobar que sacó Iker Álvarez y Diego Percan perdonó en una pelota que se le quedó muerta en el área. Entonces, en un minuto, Anuar cabeceó dentro de su portería en un córner y Percan le imitó en un gran centro de Diego Bri. El Ceuta, tocado, ya dio pocas señales de vida y Tasende, Eder García o Carracedo pudieron ampliar la renta local. Los planes que tuviera para la segunda parte José Juan Romero, que había revolucionado el once de inicio, hasta en la portería, saltaron por los aires pronto, ya que Diego Percan hizo doblete en gran pase de Eder García. El Ceuta, pese al duro marcador, no se rindió y tuvo varias ocasiones para recortar, en las botas de Escobar, Capa, Carlos Hernández o Anuar. El Córdoba también pudo ampliar su bagaje, aunque dio la sensación de regular los esfuerzos.

articles.standfirst: El central marca el gol del empate de Osasuna en el último minuto del partido
articles.summary: El central marca el gol del empate de Osasuna en el último minuto del partido
articles.body: Un gol de Catena al límite de tiempo permitió a Osasuna empatar un partido que tenía perdido y en el que el central quedaba señalado por dos errores groseros. El madrileño, que venía de una temporada compleja, se reconcilió con los aficionados y su tanto alegró sobremanera a sus compañeros, que siempre han estado muy pendientes de un futbolista de máxima importancia en el pan de Arrasate. Osasuna y Athletic lo dieron todo de su parte para que la disputa no tuviera dueño. Los de Arrasate jugaron de un modo más vertical que un Athletic que apostó por ir al pie en vez de buscar el espacio. Con el ritmo en fase alta la sensación fue que Osasuna estaba en condiciones de llegar. Pero cuando esté disminuyó el señorío del partido lo dictaba un Athletic al que penalizó su falta de profundidad. El primer portero en intervenir fue Simón, que en el 22’ sacó con el pie un disparo de Moncayola. En el otro área a Aitor se le vio diez minutos más tarde, cuando estuvo rápido para cortar un pase atrás que buscaba rematador. El portero elegido por Arrasate no lo tuvo tan claro en la siguiente jugada, cuando voló sin llegada a un zapatazo de Berenguer que se estrelló en el palo. Aitor estuvo acertado también en la última acción del primer periodo, cuando despejó un cabezazo de Yuri. Justo después el árbitro pitó el descanso y por la megafonía del estadio se escuchó la melodía del Equipo A. Una carrera contra el mundo de Budimir al punto de cumplirse la hora de batalla permitió a Osasuna liberarse de la presión a la que le estaba sometiendo el Athletic desde el inicio del segundo periodo. Los leones apretaban, pero sin sentencia, así que Osasuna no estaba por dejarse ir Y eso que casi se sacrifican después de que un tropezón de Torró habilitase a Sancet para un disparo que en condiciones normales habría entrado en 9 de cada 10 intentos. Pues bien, el de Mendillorri, que lejos de San Mamés sólo ha marcado un hat trick en El Sadar, la mandó a la grada. Osasuna no perdió ni confianza ni esperanza y sin muchas llegadas al área siempre contó con la opción de aprovechar alguna acción a balón parado. Curiosamente, la base del gol del Athletic llegó a partir de una contra tras una falta lanzada por Osasuna. La guió Iñaki Williams y ajustició Nico. El primer remate del pequeño de los Williams lo paró Aitor, pero el campeón del mundo se estiró para cazar desde el suelo el rechace. Era un gol que metía al Athletic en Europa...hasta que llegó Catena, que además marcó cuando Terzic había metido en el campo a un defensa más (Yeray) en lugar de un futbolista de ataque como Berenguer.

articles.title: El Alba se lo cree, asalta Butarque y le dedica su tercera victoria a 'Demi'
articles.standfirst: Primer triunfo a domicilio de los manchegos; Morata marcó el gol pepinero, pero Mariño le detuvo un penalti en la recta final
articles.summary: Primer triunfo a domicilio de los manchegos; Morata marcó el gol pepinero, pero Mariño le detuvo un penalti en la recta final
articles.body: El Albacete tomó aire en Butarque a costa de un Leganés que volvió a mostrar sus enormes debilidades defensivas. Y es que no sólo asaltó Butarque con un triunfo merecido, sino que firmó su tercera victoria consecutiva que le acerca a los puestos de salvación, primera a domicilio del campeonato. Los goles de Pacheco, Álex Millán e Higinio de penalti fueron contestados por el tanto de Morata, que después falló un penalti. Los pepineros, cada vez más lejos de sus aspiraciones y obligados a empezar a mirar hacia la permanencia, encadenan siete jornadas sin ganar y se queda al borde de los puestos de descenso tras un partido en cuyos prolegómenos se vivió un minuto de silencio muy emotivo y sentido en memoria de Jesús de Miguel, salido de la cantera pepinera. La primera ocasión fue visitante, con un remate alto de Lorenzo Aguado con todo a favor, fruto de la mejor puesta en escena de la escuadra de Joseba Etxeberria. El Lega, con un novedoso 4-4-2, buscaba profundidad por las bandas, pero los manchegos tomaron el control. Y así, Pacheco aprovechó la pasividad defensiva local para marcar desde fuera del área, tras avanzar muchos metros y su disparo cruzado se ‘envenenó’ tras tocar en Montero. Incluso Álex Rubio, con una vaselina que elevó demasiado ante Luca Zidane, e Higinio, con un cabezazo que salió rozando el poste, pudieron ampliar la ventaja. Gharbi y Franquesa firmaron las primeras ocasiones de un equipo pepinero que empezó a reaccionar antes de que Morata asistiera a Álex Millán para un gol que el VAR anuló por una discutible falta previa del propio Morata sobre Vallejo, dos campeones de Europa cara a cara. Y para más inri en el tiempo añadido Álex Rubio hizo el segundo, en otra acción revisada por el videoarbitraje, al resolver desde cerca un barullo en el área tras varios rechaces. Luis Carrión agitó el banquillo con tres cambios al descanso y el Leganés salió apretando. Soko pudo recortar distancias, pero el empuje duró poco. De hecho, lo que llegó fue el tercero del Alba al aprovechar Higinio el penalti cometido por Gharbi sobre Aguado, un gol que dejó muy tocados a los locales y en cuyo lanzamiento cayó lesionado el propio delantero visitante. Morata se resistió a rendirse. Y justo después de que Mariño hiciera un auténtico paradón a un cabezazo cercano de Soko, el ex capitán de la selección española recortó distancias de cabeza tras un buen envío con el exterior de Álex Sancrís y siguió tirando del equipo. Incluso provocó un claro penalti de Mariño, pero falló desde los once metros, pues el meta visitante le negó el gol con una gran estirada. Ahí murió la reacción pepinera y Mariño siguió inmenso bajo palos sacando sendos remates de Soko y Suleiman. El Albacete respiró con tres puntos de oro y dejó al Leganés sumido en una crisis cada vez más preocupante. Incluso justo antes del pitido final, Montero vio la roja directa a instancias del VAR por una entrada sobre Pacheco en la que pareció tocar el balón en primera instancia.

articles.title: Aberdeen 0-4 Hibernian: Fans turn on head coach Stephen Robinson as Hibs climb off Scottish Premiership bottom
articles.summary: Report as Hibernian earn stunning win at Aberdeen; Jamie McGrath opened scoring with superb strike before Callum Wright, Nicky Cadden and Thibault Klidje added late goals; Aberdeen supporters turned on manager Stephen Robinson as the Dons slumped to a fifth defeat in six league games.
articles.body:
Former Don Jamie McGrath opened the scoring with a superb strike just before the hour, and substitute Callum Wright lashed a second into an empty net with 10 minutes remaining.

Nicky Cadden and Thibault Klidje added late counters to round off an emphatic win at Pittodrie.

The sides had experienced differing outcomes in last week's Premier Sports Cup semi-finals, with Hibs coming from behind to beat Edinburgh rivals Hearts 2-1, while Aberdeen suffered a late defeat to Rangers.

The home side could have risen to eighth with a win while Hibs were looking to draw level with their hosts, with both sides forced into changes from their Hampden line-ups.

The ill Ayoub Mouloua and injured Emmanuel Gyamfi dropped out for Aberdeen along with Gavin Molloy, with Dan Happe preferred to the Irishman in defence. Tony Yogane and Hicham Mahou also came in.

Hibs' only change was enforced, left-back Adam Mayor dropping out through injury, but they lost captain Felix Passlack to injury within the opening 10 minutes.

Aberdeen had the better of the opening stages but Hibs keeper Raphael Sallinger remained relatively untested until he palmed away a Mahou effort after 14 minutes.

The visitors eased into the game and Martin Boyle blasted their first real effort over the bar. McGrath also saw an effort blocked by Jack Milne before clipping high and wide soon after.

Dons captain Kevin Nisbet sent a header over the bar from a Nesta Guinness-Walker cross, and Guinness-Walker would have been disappointed to see nobody latch on to his cutback soon after, the defender having dispossessed Jason Kerr.

A smart Dons move saw Nicky Devlin fizz a cross in which narrowly evaded Nisbet, before Jack Milne's 30-yard drive forced a flying save from Sallinger as the Dons turned the screw.

Milne struck the bar with a header from the resultant corner before Josh Mulligan sent a diving header wide at the other end in the final action of the opening half.

The second half opened tentatively, with Joe Newell's effort wide of the goal before Hibs took the lead in spectacular fashion.

McGrath found acres of space 25 yards out and took a touch from Newell's short pass before lashing a superb left-footed shot beyond a helpless Marius Muller, high into the top-right corner.

Aberdeen responded immediately with Conor Ronan feeding Nisbet, who saw his shot blocked, but the Irish midfielder tweaked a hamstring in the move and was forced off as the Dons made a triple substitution in chasing the game.

Hibs could have been 2-0 up soon after, Muller having to throw himself to his right to deny Mulligan.

McGrath sent another effort from close range across the face of goal while, at the other end, a teasing cross from Stuart Armstrong saw Lewis Smith's header clip the post.

But Smith blasted home Hibs' second after Muller had denied Klidje in a one-on-one, the goal sparking a loud response from the home support at their beleaguered manager.

It was all Hibs thereafter and it came as no surprise when substitute Cadden's angled drive into the bottom-left corner gave the visitors a third goal, with Klidje's stoppage-time finish from a Wright cross rubbing further salt in the wounds.

articles.title: Newport County - Walsall cup tie halted by alleged homophobic chants
articles.summary: Newport manager Hayden Mullins condemns alleged abusive chants during Saturday's FA Cup tie against Walsall.
articles.body:
The Football Association and South Wales Police could be asked to investigate alleged homophobic chants at Newport County's Rodney Parade ground.

Newport's FA Cup first round tie against Walsall on Saturday was halted for five minutes during the second half by referee Robert Massey-Ellis.

The official spoke to the managers and captains of both teams and appeared to gesture towards the home crowd close to the dugouts.

The club could still face a FA charge as homophobic and discriminatory chants breach FA rules and are also classed a hate crime.

Newport manager Hayden Mullins said after the game he had not heard any discriminatory language but said such behaviour had no place in football.

"I think it was homophobic stuff that was heard in the crowd, which is not on. We don't condone it," said Mullins.

"It was reported to the stewards and then to either the linesman or fourth official.

"I didn't hear anything, but he [the referee] has gone down the right channels, which is good. No-one wants that.

"He chose to stop play and wanted to deal with it pretty thoroughly. He wanted to make sure he was on top of that and had the right things in place, which is key."

articles.title: El emotivo discurso de Budimir en recuerdo a De Miguel: "Nos podía tocar a cualquiera..."
articles.standfirst: El delantero croata se dirigió a sus compañeros con un mensaje cargado de emoción y una dura reflexión sobre la suerte de poder disfrutar del fútbol
articles.summary: El delantero croata se dirigió a sus compañeros con un mensaje cargado de emoción y una dura reflexión sobre la suerte de poder disfrutar del fútbol
articles.body: El vestuario de Osasuna vivió uno de los momentos más emotivos de la previa de su partido ante el Athletic. Con los jugadores ya preparados para saltar al césped y vestidos con las camisetas de homenaje a Jesús de Miguel, fallecido a los 30 años, Ante Budimir tomó la palabra para dedicar unas sentidas palabras a sus compañeros. Las cámaras de Movistar+ captaron el discurso del delantero croata, que, pese a no ser el capitán, quiso compartir una reflexión que caló hondo en el vestuario. Budimir recordó que nadie es un elegido por poder disfrutar del fútbol y que todos los presentes debían sentirse afortunados por estar allí. "No llevamos esta camiseta por tenerla. Ni él (Jesús de Miguel) ni nosotros somos los elegidos. Nos podía tocar a cualquiera. Salimos al campo sabiendo que somos agraciados de estar hoy en el campo, jugando, mirando, estando en el banquillo, lo que sea. No somos elegidos, ni nosotros ni él", expresó. Poco después, los jugadores de Osasuna y Athletic, junto a los árbitros, saltaron al terreno de juego con las camisetas en memoria de De Miguel. El estadio se sumó a un sentido homenaje para recordar al atacante, en un momento marcado por la emoción y el recuerdo.

articles.title: Mestalla honró la memoria de Jesús de Miguel
articles.standfirst: El Valencia y el Real Madrid rindieron homenaje al fallecido jugador del CD Tenerife con un minuto de silencio y una parada del juego en el minuto 9
articles.summary: El Valencia y el Real Madrid honraron la memoria del jugador del CD Tenerife con un minuto de silencio y una parada del juego en el minuto 9, en una jornada de luto en todo el fútbol español
articles.body: Mestalla enmudeció antes de que rodara el balón. El Valencia y el Real Madrid rindieron homenaje este sábado a Jesús de Miguel, futbolista del CD Tenerife tristemente fallecido esta semana a los 30 años, con un sentido minuto de silencio que el estadio observó mientras su imagen presidía las pantallas del coliseo valencianista. El recuerdo había comenzado antes del pitido inicial. Los jugadores de ambos equipos saltaron al césped de forma intercalada, con una camiseta conmemorativa en la que figuraban el dorsal 9 —el que vestía el canario— y el lema "Siempre en nuestro recuerdo", y colegiado y ambos capitanes portaron un ramo de flores. Primero tuvo lugar un sentido aplauso y, acto seguido, un sentido y respetado minuto de silencio. El homenaje tuvo su momento más emotivo ya con el encuentro en marcha. En la primera interrupción posterior al minuto 9, el árbitro detuvo el juego en alusión al dorsal del futbolista. Durante esos segundos, las pantallas proyectaron un vídeo en su memoria y los futbolistas de los dos equipos, cada uno en su posición sobre el campo, se sumaron a un aplauso que recorrió las gradas de Mestalla. El gesto no se limitó a Valencia. La Real Federación Española de Fútbol, LaLiga y la Liga F acordaron que la competición siguiera su curso, pero con un reconocimiento unánime en todos los campos de LaLiga EA Sports, LaLiga Hypermotion y el resto de categorías que se disputaban este fin de semana. La Asociación de Futbolistas Españoles (AFE) había solicitado la suspensión de la jornada en señal de duelo. El Valencia, que afronta una temporada especial por tratarse de la última antes de abandonar el histórico Mestalla, quiso convertir su cita con el Real Madrid en un acto de recuerdo. Ambos clubes ya trasladaron su pésame a la familia, a los amigos y a los compañeros del futbolista, y al conjunto tinerfeño, antes de una noche en la que el fútbol pasó, por unos minutos, a un segundo plano. Mestalla también rindió homenaje a Ricardo Arias, exfutbolista del Valencia, en honor a los 50 años de su debut con el club. Por otro lado, Yulian Mosquera y Ricar Pérez, campeones del mundo sub-15 con España, gozaron de otra ovación de las gradas valencianista.

articles.summary: El uruguayo del Madrid volvió a anotar desde fuera del área para adelantar a los de Mourinho ante el Valencia

En clave madridista, estaba siendo una semana señalada para el uruguayo, que en Mestalla volvió a ocupar el lateral derecho. No evitó que sumara en ataque su segundo gol en los últimos días ya que, recordemos, fue el autor del gol que culminó la remontada blanca en Atenas ante el AEK. Mestalla no iba a librarse del arreón. Minutos después, Arda Güler puso el segundo a pase de Bellingham para restar en esperanza a los de Aguirre, que antes del 0-1 ya vieron como se les anulaba un gol por claro fuera de juego de Guido Rodríguez.

articles.title: Arch Manning Comes Up Clutch, Box Score Stats, Highlights, Draft Stock from Texas' Win vs. Mizzou
articles.summary: In what has been a roller coaster of a season for Arch Manning, the Texas standout came up huge with two second-half touchdown passes to lead the Longhorns to a 34-20 road win over No. 18 Missouri.
articles.body:
In what has been a roller coaster of a season for Arch Manning, the Texas standout came up huge with two second-half touchdown passes to lead the Longhorns to a 34-20 road win over No. 18 Missouri.

Manning endured some of the inconsistency that has been present throughout his career, but he rebounded to finish with his most passing yards in a game since the season opener against Texas State.

This was the second consecutive game for Manning with three touchdown passes and no interceptions. He has completed at least 70 percent of his attempts in three of the last four games.

Manning did a good job of keeping the offense running after Missouri would take a lead, engineering four scoring drives to tie the game after the Tigers went up. His fifth scoring drive gave the Longhorns their first lead late in the fourth quarter.

Manning dropped a dime to Raleek Brown down the sideline for a 23-yard touchdown pass that put Texas on top 27-20 with 5:03 remaining.

Another highlight of Manning's day came two possessions earlier with a 25-yard touchdown pass to Jermaine Bishop Jr. on third-and-10 in the third quarter that evened things 20-20.

After the Texas defensed forced a Missouri punt on the next possession, Manning missed a wide-open Emmett Mosley V on third-and-9 for what would have been an easy first down.

Tyler Horka of Inside Texas did note Mosley may have been more at fault for the incompletion on that play for slowing down on his route.

Manning remains an enigma for fans and draft analysts as they think about where things stand with the 2027 quarterback class.

After Manning did his part to put Texas on top, the defense really stepped up in the clutch. Mizzou went three-and-out on its next possession.

Texas was unable to run much time off the clock after getting the ball back by also going three-and-out, but the defense stepped up two plays later when Warren Roberson forced a fumble with a hit on Cayden Lee that Graceon Littleton snagged out of the air.

Brown punched the ball in on third down to seal the victory for Texas and significantly increase its chances of reaching the College Football Playoff.

The Longhorns were ranked No. 7 in the initial top 25 released on Tuesday. This marks their fourth victory over a team currently ranked in the top 20, but the schedule doesn't ease up.

Texas has another marquee road game next week against LSU in Baton Rouge. That is the Longhorns' final regular-season game against a currently-ranked opponent.

articles.title: BYU vs. Utah Final Box Score Player Stats, Highlights and CFP Poll Prediction
articles.summary: No. 3 Utah hosted No. 9 BYU for a high-stakes iteration of the Holy War on Saturday, and for the first time in the history of the rivalry, both teams entered the game ranked inside the top 10.
articles.body:
No. 3 Utah hosted No. 9 BYU for a high-stakes iteration of the Holy War on Saturday, and for the first time in the history of the rivalry, both teams entered the game ranked inside the top 10.

Although the Cougars clawed back from an early deficit, the Utes defense stifled BYU's offense in the second half to secure a 28-20 victory.

Utah quarterback Devon Dampier was involved in all four of the Utes' touchdowns, and he became the first player in NCAA history to have a game with at least 150 passing yards, 25 receiving yards, two passing touchdowns and two rushing touchdowns.

The undefeated Utes improved to 9-0 and seem destined for a bye in the College Football Playoff. BYU picked up its second conference loss and no longer controls its own destiny on the path to the Big 12 Championship. To make it to Arlington, the Cougars would need to win out and would need Texas Tech and Houston to lose at least one game each.

Utah jumped out to an early lead. The Utes capped off their opening drive with a 22-yard rushing touchdown by Dampier. They extended their lead just a few minutes later as wide receiver Braden Pegan hauled in a 46-yard touchdown.

BYU's offense began to wake up and notched a pair of field goals after pulling out a few clever trick plays.

Cougars quarterback Bear Bachmeier connected with wide receiver Legend Glasker for a 75-yard touchdown to cut Utah's lead down to 14-13.

Despite facing an early 14-point deficit, the Cougars took the lead before halftime with a four-yard rushing touchdown by running back LJ Martin.

The end of the first half was filled with drama. BYU defensive end Nusi Taumoepeau recovered a fumble to give the Cougars possession in the final two minutes, but Utes cornerback James Chenault intercepted Bachmeier in the red zone to give his team possession. The sequence didn't end in points for either team.

BYU went into halftime after scoring 20 points, but the third quarter turned ugly for the Cougars. Bachmeier threw an interception on the opening drive and failed to pick up a single first down throughout the entire quarter. Utah wasn't able to turn the interception into points as kicker Dillon Curtis missed a 29-yard attempt, but the Utes defense held BYU to a three-and-out.

Dampier connected with Pegan again on the subsequent drive — this time for a 14-yard touchdown reception — to help the Utes regain the lead.

The Utes extended their lead to eight points as Dampier found the end zone on a three-yard keeper. The score marked Dampier's fourth touchdown of the day — two through the air and two on the ground.

Bachmeier threw a crushing interception on third-and-goal from Utah's 2-yard line. Utah took possession with under five minutes remaining and alternated carries between Dampier and running back Wayshawn Parker to drain the clock.

BYU began its final possession on their own 48-yard line with 54 seconds left after the Utes managed to flip the field by just 18 yards on their punt.

Bachmeier managed to pick up a couple of first downs, but ultimately, the second half ended much like the first: A lot of drama, but no points. Bachmeier threw his fourth interception on a desperate cross-body heave into the end zone. Utah safety Nate Richie secured the interception to clinch the Utes' 28-20 victory.

articles.summary: El lateral fue el elegido por el club para hablar al descanso
articles.body: Pablo Maffeo fue el jugador del Valencia elegido para hablar en el descanso... y el defensa, caliente con el encuentro, mostró su descontento con el partido, con el árbitro y... y con la entrevista. "No me apetece nada hacer esta entrevista, es una mierda esta entrevista aquí, que no pinta nada, estamos jugando un partido... Nos pitan faltas que no son, en fin. Se hace esta entrevista y ya está, pregunta lo que quieras", contestó cuando Sergio Quirante, de Dazn, le preguntó por lo que le faltó al Valencia en la primera parte. El periodista repitió la pregunta y Maffeo contestó lo siguiente: "Que sea más justo el árbitro y ya está, no es falta en el primer gol y eso nos condiciona. Obviamente nos falta llegar al área, nos falta juego y ya está. Creo que el equipo está compitiendo bien y ya está". Maffeo se indignó sobre todo por la falta sobre Mbappé que dio lugar al primer gol del Real Madrid. El lateral desequilibró al francés y el colegiado pitó falta y le sacó amarilla. La protestó Mestalla y el valencianista y de esa falta, lanzada por Mbappé, nació el gol del Madrid, de Valverde tras recoger el rechace de la barrera.

articles.body: La Real debe hacerse fuerte en Anoeta. Europa pasa por ahí y los de Matarazzo lo saben. No es el Rayo un rival cómodo, y menos si tu jugador franquicia, Mikel Oyarzabal, llega al partido como seria duda. Es el momento para que, por tanto, Óskarsson pueda dar un paso al frente. Pasa por su mejor momento desde que llegó y es el momento idóneo para aparecer. La Real ha visto frenada su gran racha de resultados de los últimos meses, al caer en LaLiga y empatar en Europa, por lo que necesita los tres puntos para no perder más confianza. Pellegrino Matarazzo no podrá contar con Sarr, titularísimo en su defensa y que será sustituido por Jon Martín, y hasta última hora tendrá que estar pendiente del estado físico de Mikel Oyarzabal, que no entrenó ayer por estar con anginas. Remiro, Soler y Sucic apuntan a volver al once. Queda por ver si Héctor Fort y Take Kubo tienen otra oportunidad o siguen sin contar. El once rayista tendrá bajas importantes. A la de Álvaro García se le sumó la del capitán Óscar Valentín. La mejor noticia es la vuelta de Pathé Ciss, al cumplir su sanción por ciclo de amarillas, y tener a jugadores como De Frutos, Lejeune o Ratiu enrachados. Las dudas estarán en la banda. articles.title: Duke scores on 109-yard kick-6 in blowout win over NC State
articles.summary: Pellicciotta's play gave the Blue Devils a decisive 31-3 lead heading into the locker room.
articles.body:
On Saturday, Duke took another touchdown for the road before halftime, with safety Andrew Pellicciotta scoring an elusive "kick-6" to grow the Blue Devils' lead over NC State. A missed field goal led to Pellicciotta sprinting 109 yards from end zone to end zone as time expired in the first half.

After Wolfpack kicker Kanoah Vinesett's 50-yard attempt fell short with as time expired in the half, Pellicciotta was there to receive the ball deep in the end zone. The sophomore safety then sprinted downfield.

Pellicciotta juked several defenders to make the run, at one point running nearly lengthwise across the field to find space. And find space he did, making one last cut around the 30-yard line while his teammates cleared his path to the opposite end zone.

Pellicciotta's stunning cross-field run gave the Blue Devils a decisive 31-3 lead right before halftime, after Duke scored 24 points in the second quarter alone. It's a career-first touchdown for Pellicciotta, who had one interception last season after playing 12 games as a true freshman.

The Blue Devils went on to win 41-3 , a definitive victory that makes them at 4-2 in ACC play and 7-2 on the season.

The Wolfpack struggled in the loss, putting up 217 yards on offense (including just 32 on the ground) and failing to score after the first quarter despite several chances. NC State's tough performance comes two weeks after the school fired longtime head coach Dave Doeren in October.

articles.title: Maresca ‘concerned’ after Man City suffer third league loss in a row
articles.summary: Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca is concerned about his side’s form after they suffered a third Premier League defeat in a row by going down 3-1 at Nottingh...
articles.body:
Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca is concerned about his side's form after they suffered a third Premier League defeat in a row by going down 3-1 at Nottingham Forest.

City won their opening seven games of the season but followed up defeats to Aston Villa and Brighton with a poor reverse at the City Ground.

They were 2-0 down inside 18 minutes as Jair Cunha and Liam Delap scored before Rayan Cherki's fine strike after the break gave them hope.

But Delap's second on the counter-attack killed the game and left Maresca's side six points off leaders Arsenal.

"I'm always concerned, even when we win games," the Italian said. "We need to have balance. We won seven in a row. Now we have lost three in a row, so we need balance on that."

"During the international break, try to understand what we can do better, and try to start again after the international break."

"In the same way we have done the first one, we're going to use this international break to try to clarify what we can do better," he addded.

"We know we do some things better, and also we know we need to improve things. So we are going to use that and try to understand how we can avoid these kind of games," he continued.

Maresca revealed Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol were replaced at half-time due to injury.

"Both injury, both asked for a change," he said. "Marc Guehi an injury. Josko Gvardiol had some issue already during the week, so it was just because they had problems."

The victory could be a coming of age for Delap and Forest, who have struggled to adapt to life under new boss Oliver Glasner, with just one win from their opening nine games.

Delap had scored once in eight games following his club-record move from Chelsea, but his brilliant double proved he can be the man to fire Forest to better things this season.

"It's now for Liam to keep working, getting into his best shape," Glasner said. "Let's say getting back to the Liam Delap he has been at Ipswich, and then even of course improving his game and he has still a lot to improve.

"Definitely not his finishing with left and right, but he has to improve his heading, he has to improve his movements in the box.

"He has to improve his understanding what we're doing out of possession. But, also very honestly, he did very well."

Glasner reacted to Delap's second goal with a touchline sprint to join in the celebrations.

The Austrian said: "Of course, I can't demand from the players they have to outrun the opposition, and I run less than the opposite manager. So I think I had to follow.

"I just was told they were running six or seven kilometres more than City today, and that means I had to run more than Enzo Maresca as well, and I did my job. It was funny for me."

articles.title: Texas CFP resume: Longhorns strengthen case with 4th-quarter win over Missouri
articles.summary: The Longhorns got a signature win over Missouri in Week 10.
articles.body:
The No. 7 Texas Longhorns continue to pad their College Football Playoff resume. Arch Manning and the Longhorns went on the road to face a No. 18 Missouri team that had already beaten a Top-10 team in Florida earlier in the year at home.

Although the game was tied at 20-all entering the third quarter, the Longhorns impressive fourth quarter shut the door on the Tigers hopes for an upset.

Let's take a peek at how Texas got it done, and what it means for the Longhorns' CFP outlook.

How Texas' huge fourth quarter spoiled Missouri's upset hopes

Although this game had an 11 a.m. CT kickoff time in Columbia, this one was a great game. Missouri led 10-7 after the first quarter, and Texas tied things up with a 27-yard field goal to tie it at 10 a-piece by halftime.

The third quarter was a shootout, as both offenses traded field goals and touchdowns to make it 20-all entering the fourth.

Three consecutive punts by both offenses gave way to an Arch Manning touchdown pass to Raleek Brown that gave the Longhorns a 27-20 lead.

The drive was helped by a bit of a controversial call, however. What was initially ruled as a Manning fumble resulted in a 12-yard Longhorn gain and a first down:

Former referee Terry McCauley said on X that the play should have been "clearly and Obviously an incomplete forward pass."

After the score, Texas' defense forced a Missouri punt after a quick three-and-out. The Longhorns drained just 1:36 off the clock and punted the ball back to Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons with 2:06 left. Simmons had thrown for 252 yards and two touchdowns and was having a great game. But he did take a big hit on Missouri's previous drive, having to come out for a third down play before a Tigers punt.

But Texas' defense stepped up big. On 3rd-and-6, Simmons hit his receiver Cayden Lee on what looked like a first down completion. But Texas defensive back Warren Robinson popped the ball out, and it was recovered by his teammate Graceson Littleton to give Texas the ball right back.

Texas closed the door on a possible Missouri upset with an eight-yard touchdown run by Brown to make it 34-20 with 1:25 left.

Texas' big road win should boost the Longhorns' CFP hopes

Texas has two losses, but coming into this game was ranked inside the Top-10. Now with the win against Missouri, Texas now has two road wins over ranked opponents, including the Sept. 26 win over current No. 13 Tennessee. The Longhorns' biggest win is the Week 1 come-from-behind victory over then-No. 1 Ohio State. Texas also defeated No. 10 Ole Miss at home a couple weeks ago.

The Longhorns also have remaining games that can pad their resume, including next week's game on the road against LSU.

Texas' final two games will come against Arkansas at home and Texas A&M on the road. Both of those teams having losing records in the SEC. Of course, Texas' losses against unranked teams in Oklahoma and Florida aren't the best. But the number of quality wins the Longhorns have stacked up make those not matter near as much.

Don't look now, but Texas might have one of the strongest CFP resumes in the nation.

articles.title: Jason Sudeikis ‘guarantees’ Notre Dame football will upset Miami on Saturday
articles.summary: Jason Sudeikis brought a personal connection to ESPN College GameDay on Saturday, joining the broadcast as its celebrity guest picker ahead of Notre Dame’s h...
articles.body:
Jason Sudeikis brought a personal connection to ESPN College GameDay on Saturday, joining the broadcast as its celebrity guest picker ahead of Notre Dame's home matchup against Miami.

The actor and comedian appeared at Library Lawn in South Bend. Known for playing Ted Lasso and his time on "Saturday Night Live," Sudeikis drew on his family's Notre Dame ties when making his selection.

College GameDay shared the moment Saturday on X, formerly Twitter, capturing his prediction for the matchup.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Well, I have on good authority that little baby Jesus is being babysat tonight by my uncle George and by Coach Lou Holtz, and all three of them are guaranteeing a victory for the Irish, and so am I."

The broadcast's hosts dubbed the group "the four horsemen."

Sudeikis's connection to the university spans generations. His maternal grandfather graduated from Notre Dame, as did his Uncle Jim, a member of the class of 1975.

His late uncle George Wendt, who played Norm on "Cheers," attended before dropping out after his junior year. Wendt died in May 2025.

Sudeikis also attended a Notre Dame basketball camp in sixth grade and witnessed the Irish's October 15, 1988, game against Miami from the stands. That matchup later became the subject of an ESPN "30 for 30" documentary.

He found support for Saturday's pick across the panel. Nick Saban, Pat McAfee, and Kirk Herbstreit selected Notre Dame, while Desmond Howard chose Miami.

The Hurricanes and Irish hold the No. 1 and No. 11 spots, respectively, in the season's first College Football Playoff rankings.

Saturday's game kicks off at 7:30 p.m. ET/4:30 p.m. PT on NBC and Peacock, with Notre Dame seeking an upset that would strengthen its playoff resume.

articles.body: Pese a las remontadas sufridas en Champions, la Roma de Gasperini es un reloj en Serie A. El equipo capitalino sigue invicto en el campeonato italiano tras ganar 3-0 al Sassuolo en el Olímpico. Mario Hermoso, con un golazo, abrió el camino al triunfo. Roberto Aquilani, mientras, al borde del despido en un Sassuolo que acumula seis derrotas en los últimos siete partidos. Tras la decepción de Old Trafford, cuando perdieron una ventaja de 0-2 en Champions, la Roma volvió al Olímpico por la puerta grande. Recuperando a Manu Koné tras semanas de lesión, el equipo de Gasperini resolvió en la primera parte ante el Sassuolo y mantiene el pulso a Lazio e Inter en la parte alta de la clasificación. Mario Hermoso, que está haciendo una campaña digna de los mejores centrales del 'Calcio', hizo el 1-0 incorporándose al ataque y definiendo como un auténtico '10', con un disparo preciso tras un recorte. Tres minutos después, entre Malen y Walukieciwz firmaban el 2-0. Sentenció, ya en la segunda parte y quizás en el último partido sin Dybala, Rodrigo Mora con una gran jugada individual. Él y Soulé han hecho que no se eche de menos en Roma a 'La Joya' estas semanas. Un triunfo redondo del equipo de Gasperini para seguir con una temporada con muchas más alegrías que disgustos.

articles.title: Glasner glee and Delap double - win could be lift-off for Forest
articles.summary: Oliver Glasner's celebrations and two goals for Liam Delap bode well for a Nottingham Forest team looking to kick on after their first home Premier League wi...
articles.body:
The Oliver Glasner volcano could not contain the emotional lava of an impending first home Premier League victory any longer.

Nottingham Forest's opening goal from Jair Cunha against Manchester City had drawn polite applause and a sedate thumbs-up from the Austrian manager.

Glasner was bubbling below the surface after Liam Delap's strike went in - dancing a merry jig in his technical area and hoisting his fists in the air.

When Delap rattled in Forest's third goal there was an eruption of joy from the 52-year-old.

Glasner sprinted down the touchline (well, as best a man in his early fifties can sprint) to join Forest's players as they mobbed the striker.

"One of my best running stats, I guess," Glasner joked to BBC Match of the Day after Forest's 3-1 win over City.

"I will be fatigued tomorrow but I can be because it's the international break so I can have a rest."

Forest's victory was their first in the league at the City Ground this season as Glasner's philosophy finally translated into that most precious of football commodities: goals.

Perhaps he was on to something when he said his side cannot survive on "flower power" , choosing a left-field comparison of the Woodstock music festival in the 1960s.

Up to this Saturday it had been a tale of frustration.

Despite having the second-most shots in the Premier League this season (152), they had scored the fewest goals (six).

They also had the lowest shot conversion rate (4%) and biggest negative xG (-8.3).

It was telling that at full-time in this match they had scored more goals against City (three) than they had in their previous six home league games combined (two).

It was reflected in their lowly standing in the table.

Forest had the biggest negative difference between points (six) and expected points (15.49), and also the biggest positional difference based on that (19th versus third).

"I think we've had better performances in possession because today we rarely had the ball. Regarding the team spirit, the energy, I think it was our best game," Glasner said.

"The way we play football I think we've had many better games but how we defended, how passionately we defended, how tactically smart we defended, it was one of our better games."

Former Liverpool midfielder Danny Murphy said the result was a "huge moment in the season" for Forest.

"Glasner's actually been unlucky in the first part of his Forest tenure in terms of points they've got with the performances they've had," Murphy said.

"So that's a huge deal for him and the club."

Delap spent 10 years in City's academy before leaving for Ipswich in 2019.

His prolific form at Portman Road paved the way for a move to Chelsea, but he struggled to make an impact in west London and his career hit the buffers.

After managing just one goal in his first eight outings at the City Ground there were fears of regression, but he offered a timely reminder of the ability which persuaded Forest of pay £50m for him with an electric display.

With his chest puffed out, Delap took the game to City's defence, driving at them with aggression, physicality and a determination to impose himself.

"When you come in with a price tag on your back everybody believes 'if you pay so much, he has to score all the goals'," Glasner added.

"He had one great season at Ipswich then lost a lot of confidence at Chelsea, so now he's getting better and better into rhythm."

It was the first time Delap has had two shots on target in a league match this season.

He scored with two of his three attempts against City (a 67% conversion), having scored just one goal from 24 shots in his first eight games (a 4% conversion).

"As a striker it's the most important thing [to score goals]," Delap added.

"The only thing you're judged on. You can play well and not score - really nice to score. Got to keep performing and improving but today I'm happy."

Murphy said Delap, son of former Derby, Southampton and Stoke defender Rory, is going to be a "really big player" for Forest this season.

"I think in recent weeks watching him play, he's looked fit, he's looked strong, he's got himself in good positions, and today he got the rewards of some goals to add to the performance," Murphy said.

"Like any striker, he loves scoring goals, but his all-round performance was good. And if he can stay fit, his confidence grows bit by bit each week."
